# 👆 Click a mountain

This board is **one photograph with clickable zones on it** — and the zones are not ours: they are the *file's own*
[Commons image notes](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Scuol-Motta_Naluns,_11-10-2024._(actm.)_21.jpg), written
by the photographer, read out of the file's wikitext and converted to percentages of the picture. Six peaks, exactly
where that file says they are.

Hover a box (a tap reveals it on a phone) and its name appears. Clicking one **publishes the article it names** on the
card's `zones` channel, and the 📄 Article Excerpt below, listening to that channel, loads it. No page reload; the URL
never changes.

**Two channels, one picture.** Clicking the *photograph itself* publishes the **file** it shows on the card's
`selection` channel — the gallery's own behaviour — while a zone publishes the **thing it names** on `zones`. Wire a
file consumer to `selection` and an article consumer to `zones` and both work from the same picture.

**About the targets.** Only `Piz Nuna` has an article of its own on de.wikipedia; the other five peaks do not. Each of
those zones points at the **nearest thing that does** — the valley, the lakes, the list the peak appears in — chosen by
search, which is exactly the job the *suggest* step (slice C of `docs/ZONES.md`) will do for an author instead of
leaving it to memory. `Piz Mezdi`'s line ends `open`, so it opens its article in a new tab rather than feeding the card.

Zones live in the card's ⚙ panel as **text**, one per line — `x,y,w,h | label | kind | value | action`, with the box in
percentages of the picture. Fix one by hand, or write a board that has them from the start.
